department: Department of Physics (Faculty 8: Mathematics and Physics)

deadline.value: No fixed deadline; you apply as soon as you start work as academic staff or as a funded doctoral student.
deadline.quote: As soon as you start working as a member of the academic staff or, in case of scholarship holders, have been employed as a doctoral student, you have to apply for admission as a doctoral student.

gre_subject.value: The physics doctoral pages checked do not mention a GRE Subject test.

supervisor.value: A supervision declaration from the intended supervisor must be submitted with the application.
supervisor.quote: a Supervision Declaration by the intended academic supervisor has to be submitted

funding.value: Most doctoral candidates at Stuttgart already hold a paid doctoral job; this is a university-wide statement.
funding.quote: Most individual doctoral degree candidates at the University of Stuttgart already have a paid doctoral student job and work as research assistants for the University.

entry_route.value: In most cases a master's degree, Diplom or teacher's state exam is needed before admission.
entry_route.quote: In most cases, you will be accepted as a doctoral student if you have successfully completed your studies (Diplom, Master’s Degree or State Examination for Teachers)

notes: Department leaflet and doctoral page only. The physics admissions page on the faculty site is for the Master's programme (B.Sc. requirement, English test), so its English rules are not applied to the PhD. The department sets no PhD English rule, so the university record applies.
